topic: MCP Gateway Registry Comparison 2026: AWS vs Zuplo vs TrueFoundry vs Docker Gateway

key_points: Covers MCP registry taxonomy: discovery vs governance vs hosting
Compares Official MCP Registry, Smithery, Glama, MCPMarket, MCP.so
Argues that public registries alone cannot solve enterprise governance needs
Positions TrueFoundry as a unified control plane extending registry with RBAC, audit, and secrets management
Highlights shadow AI problem: agents connecting to servers without oversight

Defines 10 requirements for production MCP gateways: Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, credential brokering, capability-level filtering, virtual MCP servers, bi-directional guardrails, structured audit logs, IDP integration, SCIM provisioning
Emphasizes per-user credential brokering over pass-through token forwarding
Capability-level access control (per-tool, not per-server) as the right unit of governance
Immutable audit logs with user identity, capability type, policy decisions, failure origin
Warns against gateways that vendor-lock audit data
Establishes 2026 taxonomy: Registries (discovery) vs Gateways (routing) vs Runtimes (execution with per-user auth)
Warns against treating gateways as secure runtimes — leads to failed compliance audits
Highlights authorization intersection: Agent Permissions ∩ User Permissions = Effective Action Scope
Compares 8 platforms including Arcade, Composio, Merge, AWS AgentCore, Lunar.dev, ToolHive, Bifrost, agentgateway
Emphasizes container isolation, intent-level tools vs raw API wrappers, OpenTelemetry audit logs
Compares 12 MCP gateways across performance, governance, isolation, and compliance
Bifrost: 11µs overhead at 5,000 RPS (Go, stdio-based, fastest tested)
Lunar MCPX: finest granularity access control (global, per-service, per-tool ACLs), p99 ~4ms
ToolHive: strongest isolation (container-level, token optimization 60-85% reduction)
agentgateway: Linux Foundation, CEL policy engine, Rust-based, OAuth 2.1 mandatory
Positions MCP gateways as complementary to LLM routing gateways
Covers TrueFoundry, Docker, IBM ContextForge, Microsoft, Lasso Security, Lunar MCPX, MintMCP
TrueFoundry: sub-3ms latency, unified LLM+MCP control plane, RBAC, HIPAA/GDPR, containerized deployment
Docker: container-isolated MCP servers, signed images, security-first, Docker Desktop integration, but less enterprise governance
IBM ContextForge: federation, multi-gateway deployments, virtual server composition, alpha/beta stage
Microsoft: Azure-native, Entra ID auth, API Management, Azure Monitor, but vendor lock-in risk
Lasso Security: AI-native security, threat detection, plugin-based architecture, Gartner Cool Vendor 2024

MCP.so lists over 19,000 MCP servers as of 2026
MCPMarket.com lists over 10,000 MCP servers across 23+ categories
Smithery hosts over 7,000 MCP servers as the closest equivalent to Docker Hub for MCP
Bifrost achieves 11 microseconds overhead per request at 5,000 RPS sustained
TrueFoundry achieves sub-3ms latency under load with in-memory authentication and rate limiting
Lunar MCPX reports p99 latency overhead around 4ms
ToolHive reduces token usage by 60-85% per call using hybrid semantic and keyword search tool filtering
MCP was adopted by every major AI vendor including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft by 2026
Cisco announced dedicated MCP security tooling at RSA Conference 2026
MCP gateways as a category emerged approximately 12 months before mid-2026
Portkey being acquired by Palo Alto Networks for MCP gateway capabilities in 2026

angles: MCP gateways became a distinct category in 2025-2026, evolving from thin auth proxies to full governance platforms — this is the first comprehensive comparison of the four major approaches

Four distinct architectural philosophies: AWS (cloud-native ecosystem lock-in), Zuplo (API gateway heritage with capability-level policies), TrueFoundry (unified LLM+MCP control plane), Docker (container-isolation-first)
The registry vs gateway vs runtime taxonomy is critical for enterprise buyers — many products conflate these layers
Per-user authorization (OBO/OAuth 2.1) is the key differentiator between hobbyist and production-grade gateways in 2026
Shadow AI is the new shadow IT — MCP gateways are the access control layer that prevents ungoverned agent-tool connections
Open-source options (Bifrost, ToolHive, agentgateway) compete with enterprise platforms (TrueFoundry, Zuplo, AWS) on different axes — performance vs governance vs ecosystem
